5-6.title: Relate Partial Products to an Algorithm

questions.title: Be Curious · What do you notice? What do you wonder?
questions.hint: Compare the two ways 132 × 3 is written.
steps: Look at the left problem: it shows three partial products, 300, 90 and 6.
Look at the right problem: it shows only the final product.
Notice that both give 396, then write a question you wonder about.
questions.answer: Sample answer: I notice both ways get 396. The left one shows each partial product (3 × 100, 3 × 30, 3 × 2) and the right one only shows the answer. I wonder how you can get 396 without writing the partial products.
questions.verification: Original page visually checked; 132 × 3 = 396 computed in Python; 300 + 90 + 6 = 396 checked by adding.

questions.title: Learn · Los Angeles to New York City
questions.hint: The map shows Los Angeles to Phoenix is 413 miles.
steps: Multiply the ones, tens and hundreds, regrouping when needed.
Write the product with the unit: miles.
questions.verification: Original page visually checked; Computed 413 × 7 = 2,891 in Python; checked by estimate 400 × 7 = 2,800.

questions.title: Math is… Generalizations
questions.hint: Compare the partial products for 413 × 7 with the steps of the algorithm.
steps: The algorithm finds the same pieces, one place value at a time.
Instead of writing each piece, it regroups and writes one product.
questions.answer: Sample answer: Both multiply each place value of 413 by 7 (2,800 + 70 + 21 = 2,891). The algorithm does the same multiplying but regroups as it goes, so it writes only one product instead of adding the partial products at the end.
questions.verification: Original page visually checked; 2,800 + 70 + 21 = 2,891 checked in Python; matches algorithm result 413 × 7.

questions.title: 13 · Extend Your Thinking
questions.hint: Think about what goes wrong if you skip regrouping.
steps: Each step multiplies one place value.
Regrouped digits must be added in the next step.
Skipping or mixing up a step gives the wrong product.
questions.answer: Sample answer: Each step multiplies a different place value and passes the regrouped tens, hundreds or thousands to the next step. If you skip a step or forget to add the regrouped amount, a place value is left out and the product is wrong. For example, 413 × 7 is 2,891, but forgetting the 2 regrouped tens gives 2,871.
questions.verification: Original page visually checked; Explanation prompt; example checked: 413 × 7 = 2,891 in Python, and omitting 20 gives 2,871.

questions.title: Reflect · Partial products and an algorithm
questions.hint: Think back to 132 × 3 on the Be Curious page.
steps: Partial products show each place value multiplied separately.
The algorithm multiplies the same place values, regrouping as it goes.
questions.answer: Sample answer: They both multiply each place value of the number. Partial products write each product (300 + 90 + 6 = 396) and then add, while the algorithm regroups as it goes and writes only the final product, 396.
questions.verification: Original page visually checked; 132 × 3 = 396 and 300 + 90 + 6 = 396 checked in Python.
